does: Beats a slice of meat to an even, thin sheet between layers of paper, so that it cooks in moments and stays tender.

intro.what: A meat slice is gently beaten between paper into an even sheet without tears.
intro.why: The aim is consistent thickness rather than maximum thinness. Working from the middle prevents a thick centre surrounded by fragile edges.

how: Trim away any sinew or skin from the slice, and nick the edge in a few places so that it does not curl.
Lay the slice between sheets of parchment paper.
Beat it from the middle outwards with the flat of a heavy pan, in even blows, turning it as you go.
Stop when the sheet is the same thickness from edge to edge, before it tears.

cues.text: The slice is an even sheet with no thick middle and no holes.
Under the pan the meat gives evenly and no longer springs back.

mistakes.mistake: Beating with hard, sharp blows that tear the meat into holes.
mistakes.fix: Use the flat of the pan, with steady, even weight.

mistakes.mistake: Beating the edges thin and leaving the middle thick, so that it cooks unevenly.
mistakes.fix: Start in the middle and work outwards.

quiz.question: Why aim for even thickness across the slice?
choices: To keep a thicker centre that supports the thinner edges.
To avoid a thick centre cooking differently from thin edges.
To roughen the surface without changing its thickness.
quiz.because: Consistent thickness reduces the contrast between the centre and edges during cooking.

quiz.question: Where should the flattening strokes begin?
choices: At the edges until they become very thin.
Only at a corner of the slice.
quiz.because: Starting centrally addresses the thick part before working toward the edges.

quiz.question: What should the flattened slice look like?
choices: Torn edges around a thick centre.
A narrow strip with punctures throughout.
quiz.because: An unbroken even sheet shows that the pressure has spread rather than torn the meat.

quiz.question: Sharp hard blows tore holes in the meat. What would you change on the next slice?
choices: Use sharper impacts on the torn areas.
Use the flat of the pan with steady even pressure.
Keep striking the thinnest edges hardest.
quiz.because: Broad controlled pressure spreads the meat without concentrating the impact into tears.

comes_after.why: Sinew and skin are cut away first, or they shrink and curl when the meat is beaten flat.
